sections.h2: What is the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds office for?
sections.html:
It is the county's public archive for land and business filings. Staff take in documents for registration, index them, and store them so anyone can trace ownership of a Charlotte lot or a Davidson farmhouse.

On the real estate side the county names conveyances, deeds of trust, mortgages, powers of attorney, assumed business names, separation agreements and plats. The counter also issues marriage licenses, swears in notaries, records military discharge papers, and holds vital records.

Holiday closings are posted on the office website, so check it before you plan a trip downtown.

sections.h2: How far back do Mecklenburg County land records go?
sections.html:
The county runs two databases. The modern one holds real estate documents added from March 1990 to the present, and the historic one holds land records and images from 1763 through February 1990. Staff also keep physical records available for inspection at the office from half past eight to half past four.

A title searcher working on an old Mecklenburg parcel often needs both sides of that 1990 line: a recent deed of trust in the modern index and an older chain of conveyances in the historic one. Before you list an inherited house, search your parcel under the family name and the previous owner's name to see what is still of record, such as an unreleased mortgage.

sections.h2: Why does the recording time of a Mecklenburg deed matter?
sections.html:
Registration decides who stands first. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance does not defeat lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is registered where the land lies, and rank follows the order of filing.

For a Mecklenburg seller that means a creditor's claim could still beat the buyer until the new deed is indexed. Ask your closing attorney when the package goes in.

sections.h2: What does the county charge to record documents?
sections.html:
Mecklenburg posts a Uniform Fee Schedule that tracks G.S. 161-10. The two amounts sellers meet most are below, and each added page past the allowance costs $4.

Mecklenburg Register of Deeds, fees most often paid on a sale

Deed and other general instruments$26 for 15 pages
Loan security instrument$64 for 35 pages
Document outside format rules$25 extra
Mortgage satisfactionFree

A certified copy costs $5 for page one and $2 for the rest. Plain copies cost 25 cents a page at the counter or $1 by mail. A plat is $21 a sheet, and each extra instrument in one filing is $10. Party names past twenty cost $2 each in index fees.

sections.h2: What format does a Mecklenburg County filing need?
sections.html:
G.S. 161-14(b) sets the layout, and a document that misses it is accepted for the $25 surcharge. The county's checklist covers five points.

  • Paper size: 8.5 inches wide, 11 or 14 inches tall.
  • Margins: three open inches above the text on sheet one, a quarter inch elsewhere.
  • Type: black on white, nine points or larger, with pen allowed for blanks and corrections.
  • Sides: printed on one side only.
  • Heading: a label for the kind of instrument on the first sheet.

Run a document you drafted yourself against this list before submitting it.

sections.h2: What is the tax on a Mecklenburg County deed, and who covers it?
sections.html:
The seller carries this cost. G.S. 105-228.30 sets one dollar for each $500 of price, with part of a $500 block rounded up, and the office collects it before it records the deed.

The county keeps one half and the state receives the other. Your settlement statement shows the dollar figure for your sale price.

Census figures show 1,233,383 residents in mid 2025, and 2020 to 2024 data show a middle owner value of $406,800. Owners live in 55.1 percent of homes, and median rent is $1,627, so a big share of housing is rented.

sections.h2: What should a seller check in the records before listing a Mecklenburg County house?
sections.html:
Look at three places, because each answers a different question. The Register of Deeds shows what is recorded against the parcel, the county's property record card shows how Tax Administration describes the house, and the Tax Collector shows what is owed.

  • Recorded deeds of trust with no matching satisfaction. A paid-off loan can still look open if the lender never filed its release.
  • The name on the latest deed. On an inherited property, the last recorded owner is often the person who died.
  • The property record card at Reval.MeckNC.gov, which lists bedrooms, bathrooms and other characteristics the county uses to value the house.
  • The county's no-cost alert service, so a later filing under your name reaches you.

A closing attorney will run a full title search in any event. Doing a light version first tells you whether a sale will be quick or whether an old lien, a missing release or an unprobated estate has to be cleared up before closing.

sections.h2: What steps carry a signed deed to the public record?
sections.html:
Four steps get a deed from signature to the public index. The state treats its fee list as complete and exclusive, so payment is due when you file.

  • Match the grantor's name and legal description to the prior deed.
  • Have the seller's side cover the excise tax.
  • Add the page-count fee and any surcharge.
  • Hand in the original and keep proof that it was recorded.

A lender's satisfaction after payoff is recorded free and will show up in the index afterward.

sections.h2: Where do veterans and homeowners go for other filings?
sections.html:
Discharge papers are recorded at this office, and the county has 44,881 veterans in Census survey data for 2020 through 2024. A property tax break for disabled veterans is another matter: applicants complete Form NCDVA-9 with a Veterans Service Officer and file with the county assessor. The exclusion covers $45,000 of value and has no age or income cutoff.

The register is an elected county officer, chosen every two years under G.S. 161-1. Questions about deed contents or title for a specific house belong with a closing attorney. Value and exemption questions go to Tax Administration.

sections.h2: How can I pay, and how do I guard my title?
sections.html:
At the counter the office takes cash, Mastercard, Visa and Discover, checks, money orders, and approved escrow accounts. Checks need a printed name and address and a phone number, and they go to the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds. Starter and counter checks are turned away, and a bounced check may cost $35.

The office offers a no-cost Property Fraud Alert that notifies you when any document under your name reaches the records, which suits owners of vacant or inherited houses. Anyone buying on a contract for deed should know Chapter 47H obliges the seller to record the contract, or a memorandum of it, inside five business days.

If you own a Mecklenburg house burdened by back taxes, a title snag or a difficult tenant, a cash buyer can set a closing date that works and use a closing attorney for the recording.

faqs.q: What does Mecklenburg County bill for filing a deed?
faqs.a: $26 covers the first fifteen pages, plus $4 for each page past that. A loan instrument costs $64 for thirty-five pages. Documents outside the format rules carry a $25 surcharge.

faqs.q: Which party pays the deed stamp tax in a Mecklenburg sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. The rate is one dollar per $500 of price, rounded up for a partial block, and it is due at the counter.

faqs.q: Does recording a mortgage satisfaction cost anything?
faqs.a: No charge applies. The fee schedule lists satisfaction instruments as free, so the burden is only to confirm your lender files one after payoff.

faqs.q: Can I look up Mecklenburg land records on my own?
faqs.a: Yes. A modern online database covers documents from March 1990 forward, a historic index covers 1763 through February 1990, and records can be inspected at the office from half past eight to half past four.

faqs.q: What happens to a deed that breaks the format rules?
faqs.a: It is still recorded, but you pay $25 on top of the usual fees. Margins, tiny type and two-sided pages cause most of those cases.
